title: search_structure input
description: Code found by its shape, with ast-grep's pattern syntax over the syntax tier's Tree-sitter grammars (FR1060): every await in a loop, every call of escape with a string, every catch that swallows its error. Optionally only inside the symbols reachable from or reaching a symbol, or the files importing a file (scope). Read-only, over the snapshot's captured content, not the working tree. Lean over MCP: one `<enclosing name> <path>:<line> "<first line of the match>"` row per match, the text cut at 120 characters; pages with a cursor, and completion.total counts every match. Time, matches and bytes are the usual limits; files over 1 MiB are not parsed.

repository_id.description: Optional when exactly one repository is registered.

snapshot_id.description: Null pins the current published snapshot.

freshness.description: snapshot (default) answers from the published snapshot. strict first checks that the working tree is exactly what the snapshot was built from; if not, it starts an index and refuses with STALE_INPUT naming the changed files.

envelope.description: lean, the default over MCP: plain text with no JSON and no structuredContent. A header `# <tool> · <n> rows · <snapshot> current` (stale when the snapshot is older than the repository's current one), one `<name> <path>:<line>` row per result, then `# ` lines for the limitations of this answer and `# more: cursor <c>` when a next page exists. The line is the call, import or reference site for relationship, impact and path rows and the declaration for symbol rows; tags follow: in or out when both directions are asked, depth=<n>, dispatch, external, candidate, ambiguous, unresolved:<reason>, and the relationship type when the query mixes types. A name or path with a space, quote or # is quoted as JSON. compact: the JSON envelope without the snapshot-wide parts an earlier answer gave (coverage, unresolved reasons, standing limitations). full: the whole JSON envelope. Ask for compact or full for ids, evidence and totals.

cursor.description: The next_cursor of the previous page. It continues the same query on the same snapshot; it expires after an hour.

pattern.description: Code in the language, with ast-grep's metavariables: $X matches one node, $$$X (or $$$) any number of nodes, $_ one node without capturing, $$X an unnamed node too. A repeated metavariable must match equal code. Matching is ast-grep's default (smart): comments and punctuation the pattern leaves out are skipped. A pattern that does not parse is refused with the parse error and its syntax tree.

language.description: The pattern's language: only files with its extensions are searched, as ast-grep chooses them (typescript: .ts .cts .mts; tsx; javascript, read with the TSX grammar; python; go; ...). Omitted: every file whose extension has a grammar here, with the pattern parsed in each file's language; a language it does not parse in is skipped and named, and files with no grammar are counted.

path_prefix.description: Only files whose repository-relative path starts with this. Default: the whole repository.

scope.description: Only matches inside what the graph names; several keys intersect. A match counts when a symbol of the scope holds it whole.

items.description: A symbol id (sym_...), a name the snapshot holds once (`DataSource.initialize`, as a lean row shows it, or a plain name), or { name, path }.

reachable_from.description: Symbols, each with every symbol trace_paths reaches from it (resolved calls, and dispatch both ways through implements and overrides), within max_depth.

items.description: A symbol id (sym_...), a name the snapshot holds once (`DataSource.initialize`, as a lean row shows it, or a plain name), or { name, path }.

reaching.description: Symbols, each with every symbol that reaches it the same way, within max_depth.

importing.description: Repository-relative file paths: only matches in the files whose resolved imports name one of them.
